correctness.rationale: Independent inspection of Ma arXiv:2610.00193v1, Theorem 2.3 (2.15)-(2.18), confirms bounded B, the operator defect Q=R+sum lambda_r v_r v_r*, and exact finite-support right inverse ML=I; source polynomials p_{m,r} match the package. Density of M(c00) reduces sharp ratio to weighted R-Rayleigh infimum on c00, with strictly positive r_n. As n->infty, r_n=m^2/n+O(n^-2), v_0~1/n gives divergent sum |v0|^2/r_n, while v_r=O(n^-r-1), r>=1 gives convergent weighted Gram. For alpha>0 the positive unbounded weighted-functional rank-one term can be killed by increasingly distant finite-support tails at arbitrarily small R-norm: kernel dense in weighted completion, so omitting it does not change infimum. Then the remaining bounded weighted finite-rank selfadjoint operator has nonzero spectrum that of G^(1/2) Lambda G^(1/2), and the infinite-dimensional orthogonal complement supplies eigenvalue zero; hence 1+min(0,lambda_min). For -1<alpha<0, truncating R^-1 v0 drives negative lambda0 Rayleigh quotient to -infinity while other rank-one terms are weighted bounded. alpha=0 all lambdas zero. At m=2, G11 digamma telescoping and lambda1=3alpha(alpha^2-1) give explicit value; order-two Cauchy-Schwarz nonattainment in 0<alpha<1 follows because R^-1 v1 is not orthogonal to v0. Independently re-evaluated 20,000 positive summands at alpha=1/2 giving c=0.9859318143428387 versus 261/560+3 log2/4=0.9859318139913875 with positive truncation difference 3.52e-10. Finite test does not prove the all-order analytic identity. Boundary m=1 uses empty matrix convention.
